data.value: Runs the background processing — ESI polling, pricing, contracts, alarms, the scheduler and backups — without EVE Console being open. Exactly one client does this work: if this app is open and already doing it, the unit waits and takes over when you close it.

data.name: SvcIntroWindows
data.value: Runs the background processing — ESI polling, pricing, contracts, alarms, the scheduler and backups — without EVE Console being open, starting automatically with Windows. data.name: SvcInstallNoteSystemd
data.value: Installed as a systemd user unit in ~/.config/systemd/user, so no root access and no password prompt. It runs as you, inside your login session, which is how it reaches your keyring for the saved database password — and why it starts when you log in rather than when the machine boots. For a machine that boots unattended, see the system unit in the project's packaging directory.
data.comment: Polling tab, background service on Linux. Keep the folder path ~/.config/systemd/user as it is.

data.name: SvcInstallNoteWindows
data.value: Installing and removing ask for administrator approval once; starting and stopping afterwards do not. The service runs as LocalSystem, so a copy of the database connection is written to C:\ProgramData\EveConsole for it to read — that copy can be decrypted by anything running on this computer, unlike the one saved for your account. Removing the service deletes it.
data.comment: Polling tab, background service on Windows. LocalSystem is a Windows account name; keep it and the folder path.

data.value: How long EVE Console keeps data it can afford to forget. Only the agent's own record is purged by default — every other rule is off until you turn it on — and an enabled rule runs once a day. Purging removes rows, but SQLite reuses the freed pages rather than returning them, so the file itself only gets smaller after a compaction — see Database → Shrink Database. Database → Storage Breakdown shows where the space actually went.

data.name: RetentionKillmailsNote
data.value: Removes the kill and everything attached to it — attackers, items, references and zKillboard flags. Kill mails and their indexes are the largest thing in a typical database (61% of a measured 4 GB file), so these are the rules that actually reclaim space. Two rules, so your own history can be kept longer than everyone else's; each is off until you turn it on. ⚠️ Deleted kills are gone locally; getting them back means re-fetching from ESI or zKillboard, and ESI only serves recent ones.
